prompt: React vs Vue: which should I learn first?

plan.title: React vs Vue: Which Should You Learn First?
plan.description: A fair comparison of React and Vue for beginners, judged on learning curve, ecosystem and jobs, and your own goals. Find out which one fits your situation.

beats.narration: You want to build modern websites, and everyone tells you something different. Learn React. No, learn Vue. What if the popular answer is not the best answer for you?

props.title: React or Vue?
props.subtitle: Which one should you learn first?

beats.narration: Both are JavaScript tools for building user interfaces. Both break a page into small reusable pieces called components. So the real difference is not what they do, but how they feel to use.
Let's judge them on three things. First, the learning curve. Second, the ecosystem and jobs. Third, which one fits your goals. Keep these three in mind as we go.
Vue is often described as gentle for beginners. Its templates look like ordinary HTML, and its structure is clear. You can get something working quickly, which keeps motivation high.
React asks you to think more in JavaScript. You write markup inside your code, which feels strange at first. But once it clicks, many people find it flexible and very consistent.
React has a very large community, and many companies use it. That usually means more tutorials, more libraries and more job listings. Vue is smaller, but it is well loved and has solid tools.
Job markets differ by country and city, so check listings where you live. Look at what local employers ask for, because that is the honest way to decide.
Here is the good news. Skills transfer. Components, state and data flow work in both. Learn one well, and the second takes weeks, not months.

props.text: Learn one well, and the second comes much faster.

beats.narration: So decide by situation. If you want the most job options, pick React. If you want a smooth start or a personal project, pick Vue.
The takeaway: do not agonize. Pick one today, build a small project this week, and finish it. Finishing a project teaches more than any debate ever will.
